newsitem.title: UK: Guardian says considering major buy.
newsitem.headline: Guardian says considering major buy.

text.p: Insurance group Guardian Royal Exchange Plc on Tuesday said it was considering a major acquisition within the next 12 months, possibly in the life sector.
The company told industry analysts that a UK life acquisition was top of the list, that it could comfortably fund a one billion pound acquisition and would be prepared to spend more if necessary.
Worries that the acquisition might be in the life sector which would probably necessitate a goodwill write-off knocked the shares lower in afternoon trading.

After an initial rise on the back of the figures, the shares lost ground to be 6-1/2 pence lower at 281-1/2 pence by mid-afternoon on news of the plans and disappointment that the company had no plans to return capital to shareholders through a special dividend or buyback.

"We have got a strong balance sheet. We do believe this year there will be a number of opportunities to use it to grow the business rather than give it back in a tax inefficient way," said a spokesman for Guardian.

"There are a number of opportunities to grow the business not only in the UK and U.S. We have stated our intention to grow the business in three principal areas -- UK general, UK life and health and the other is U.S. general."
Guardian is not a major player in the UK life market and an acquisition could give them critical mass and economies of scale, commented one analyst.
Earlier as expected by analysts, Guardian reported sharply lower earnings, blaming continued competition and the worst catastrophe weather claims in the U.S. for 75 years for fall in profits.
